neighbours.label: a kinship or close-relation noun after a possessive (his mother, his extended family, her siblings, his intimate friends)
fire: After the trial he learned that the witness was his mother.
He sends most of his wages home to support his extended family.
She spent the holidays with her siblings in the countryside.
He confided only in his intimate friends about the illness.
The child clung tightly to her father at the station.
They invited their cousins to the wedding in June.
The old man left the farm to his grandson.
She wrote a letter every week to her sister abroad.
quiet: After the trial he learned that the witness was lying.
He sends most of his wages home to pay off the mortgage.
She spent the holidays alone in the countryside.
He confided only in a diary about the illness.
The child clung tightly to the railing at the station.
They invited the whole office to the party in June.
The old man left the farm to the local church.
She wrote a letter every week to the newspaper.
